question: Does `Erdos945.erdos_945.variants.equivalence : Erdos945Prop ↔ Erdos945Constant` hold for the exact definitions at FC commit `9c4d5821819656af53c5473ded2116ea14a7ff1c`?
proposed_result: Yes, the exact formulations are mathematically equivalent, but a complete Lean term was not built. For `Erdos945Prop → Erdos945Constant`, eventual `O =O 1` gives a constant K with `|O x| ≤ K`. Choose C substantially larger than K, e.g. K+2. If `[x,x+(log x)^C]` had no equal-τ pair, put `n = ⌈x⌉₊-1` and `k = ⌊x+(log x)^C⌋₊-n`. Then `Set.Ioc n (n+k)` is τ-injective, `n+k ≤ y := x+(log x)^C`, and hence `k ≤ F y`. But eventually `k ≥ (log x)^C-1`, whereas `F y ≤ (log y)^K`; since C>K and `log(x+(log x)^C) ∼ log x`, this is impossible. For `Erdos945Constant → Erdos945Prop`, let C>0 and X be an eventual threshold. Any admissible τ-injective block `Set.Ioc n (n+k)` ending at most y either begins beyond X, in which case applying the duplicate property at `x=n+1` forces `k < 1+(log(n+1))^C ≤ 1+(log y)^C`, or begins before X, in which case applying it at a fixed sufficiently large point at or above X bounds the block by a constant depending only on X and C. Thus `F y ≤ max(B,1+(log y)^C)` eventually, which is at most `(log y)^(C+1)` after increasing the threshold. Taking `O` to be the constant function C+1 proves `Erdos945Prop`.

evidence.observation: The selection check identifies this exact target as proof/search, requires all of `945.lean`, records source SHA-256 `7caf8d1ea9efca08a6ec421c7fb4526f4ad626feb08775d9b6e8c56fa6d3cf41`, and reports no prior target packet or target-level `formal_proof`.
`F x = sSup {k | ∃ n, n+k ≤ x ∧ (Set.Ioc n (n+k)).InjOn τ}`. Thus an admissible block contains exactly k natural-number points and excludes n while including n+k.

`Erdos945Prop` quantifies a real-valued exponent function `O` satisfying `O =O[atTop] 1` and eventually `(F x : ℝ) ≤ log x ^ O x`; this supplies an eventual uniform absolute bound on the exponent, not a literal constant exponent.

`Erdos945Constant` quantifies C>0 and eventually demands distinct naturals a,b in the closed real interval `[x,x+(log x)^C]` with equal τ-values. The endpoint mismatch with `F` is handled by starting the integer block at `⌈x⌉₊-1` in the forward direction and applying the closed-interval property at `n+1` in the reverse direction.
No existing proof of the equivalence was found; only the target declaration with `sorry`, the selection material, and references to the declaration were found.

build_or_check_outcome: No repository modification and no Lean build were performed. The exact source bytes and SHA-256 were checked, and both mathematical directions were analyzed with the `Ioc`/`Icc` endpoint and cardinality shifts accounted for.
assumptions_and_dependencies: Standard eventual consequences of `O =O[atTop] 1`: existence of K≥0 with `|O x|≤K` for all sufficiently large x.
Eventual monotonicity and growth facts for real `log` and real powers, including `(log x)^C-1 > (log(x+(log x)^C))^K` when C>K.
Natural floor/ceiling lemmas identifying the naturals in a closed real interval with an `Ioc` block.
`Nat.sSup` boundedness/least-upper-bound lemmas allowing a uniform bound on every admissible k to bound `F y`.

The fixed-threshold case in the reverse implication requires choosing a real threshold suitable for the eventual statement and then bounding all blocks beginning below it by one fixed duplicate-bearing interval.
limitations: This is a proof blueprint rather than a checked Lean proof.
The required analysis and floor/ceiling library lemmas were not assembled into a compiling term.
No claim is made that the equivalence already exists elsewhere beyond the inspected reachable sources.
smallest_independent_check: Formalize two local lemmas: (1) if τ is injective on naturals in `[x,z]`, then with `n=⌈x⌉₊-1` and `k=⌊z⌋₊-n`, the pair `(n,k)` belongs to the set defining `F z`; (2) under `Erdos945Constant`, every admissible `(n,k)` ending at y satisfies eventually `k ≤ max(B,1+(log y)^C)`. These isolate the only endpoint/cardinality work; standard asymptotic estimates then close the equivalence.
